clue.text: Trumpeter's one was back to front and short

indicators.note: the word's back letter is brought round to its front, so the last letter leads

parts.note: taken as written
and shortened to 'n, as in fish 'n' chips

explanation.surface: Someone playing the trumpet once had their instrument the wrong way round and came up short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpeter' looks like a musician, but the trumpeter is a species of large North American bird, and the answer is the kind of bird it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpeter is a species of large white waterbird, so one trumpeter is an example of this bird.

clue.text: Make good operational cuts, as bent police officer might

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sew closed the incisions made during surgery
second meaning: frame an innocent person, as a corrupt officer might do

explanation.walkthrough: A surgeon closing wounds and a corrupt cop framing a suspect share the same phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to sew a wound closed and, informally, to frame someone with false evidence.

clue.text: Nick accepts barber's final cut

indicators.note: one word takes the other letter inside it, as if accepting it

parts.note: to nick a criminal is to arrest, or cop, them
the final letter of the word barber

explanation.surface: A barber in Nick's shop gives the last haircut of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name; it is a verb meaning to arrest. 'Cut' as a noun here is a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop is a very short haircut, so the word is a synonym for a close cut of the hair.

clue.text: Supporter of triumphant Wimbledon winner removing top?

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: the champion at Wimbledon holds the trophy, so is the cup holder

explanation.surface: A fan of the victorious Wimbledon champion takes off a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; its winner holds the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholder is one who maintains or backs something, a synonym for a supporter.

clue.text: Aphrodisiac found in bed?

parts.note: reads as a love aid in the bedroom; really a shellfish reputed to stir desire, which grows on a seabed colony called a bed

explanation.surface: A sexual stimulant turns up between the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a shellfish bed on the sea floor, not one in a bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: This shellfish is famously reputed to stimulate desire and is farmed in seabed colonies called beds.

clue.text: After ten rounds men part, resorting to an underhand tactic

indicators.note: the second rearranged piece comes after the first
the three letters are turned round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: re-sorting, putting these letters in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: After ten rounds of boxing the fighters separate, and one turns to dirty tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Luring someone into committing an offence they would not otherwise commit is a sly, deceitful ploy.

clue.text: A twice-married woman's outside clobber

indicators.note: the woman's word sits around the other letters

parts.note: her is the word for a woman's

indicators.note: the married letter comes two times

explanation.surface: A woman who has wed twice wears her gear on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: HER goes round A plus two Ms; 'clobber' is the verb, to hit hard, not the British slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To hammer someone is to beat or thrash them, the same sense as to clobber.

clue.text: Rabbit caught by deerstalker?

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a deerstalker is a tweed cap, an example of headwear

explanation.surface: A rabbit is snared by someone stalking deer.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit is British slang for talking at length, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit is British informal slang for talking idly, the same as to natter or converse.

clue.text: Hose with tear needing repair?

indicators.note: the torn word must be fixed by putting its letters back in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden hose with a split in it needs mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' looks like a noun; it is the verb to spray with liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: To hose a garden is to spray it with liquid, the verb meaning to irrigate.

clue.text: You'll have got ready to settle thus

definitions.text: You'll have got ready to settle thus

parts.words: You'll have got ready to settle thus
parts.note: reads as being prepared to resolve a matter; ready is slang for money, and settling a bill with it means handing over notes and coins

explanation.surface: You'll have prepared yourself in order to resolve matters this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got ready' seems to mean prepared, but 'the ready' is old slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling a bill with notes and coins requires having money on you, which is what 'ready' means in slang.

clue.text: Unable to meet the challenge in bed, turn over one time

parts.note: someone still in bed is not up
TO is a dictionary abbreviation for turn over, as on a page or in business turnover
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone in bed, unable to rise to the occasion, rolls over once more.
explanation.walkthrough: TO for turn over is listed in Chambers; it is the PTO on a page without the 'please'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means lacking the ability or energy for a task, i.e. incapable of meeting it.

clue.text: Blinking fast Italian's short despatch

parts.note: REM, rapid eye movement, the darting of the eyes during dreaming sleep
It is the short form of Italian, as in gin and It (Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: An Italian, fluttering their eyelids, sends off a terse message.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send, as in remitting payment, so it means to dispatch or forward.

clue.text: Entering a quiet sea, one's sheepish

indicators.note: the call for silence and the second letter go into the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
sh is the call for silence
one gives A, the indefinite article meaning one; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Someone wading quietly into the sea feels embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sheepish means feeling awkward and embarrassed over something one has done.

clue.text: Mouldy stuff, when applied to reduced image

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

indicators.note: the word for an image is cut short to its slang abbreviation

parts.note: a picture is an image

explanation.surface: Mould spreads over a photograph that was shrunk down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouldy' here means set in a mould, not rotten: this savoury jelly is shaped in moulds.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly set in a mould, so it is literally moulded stuff.

clue.text: It comes with strings: in short, that is no matter, maybe

indicators.note: perhaps these letters belong in another order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: An offer that comes with conditions attached, in short, may not matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes with strings' suggests a conditional deal, but the strings are literal ones worked from above.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a puppet operated by strings attached to its limbs.

clue.text: Accounts ultimately for energy drinks

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken
port is a fortified wine, so ports are drinks

explanation.surface: Records reveal what is spent, in the end, on energy drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports are accounts given of events, a synonym in the sense of descriptions or narratives.

clue.text: Clip of second try

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it

explanation.surface: A short excerpt from a second attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear is to cut or trim, as with sheep's wool, so it matches clip as a verb.

clue.text: English artist who can decorate cakes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: John ..., the twentieth-century English painter
second meaning: one who pipes icing on to cakes

explanation.walkthrough: John Piper was an English painter known for stained glass and wartime scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the painter John Piper is also the term for someone who squeezes icing through a nozzle.

clue.text: Deer's on loose — evidence of cold?

indicators.note: the letters are let loose and run free into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A deer has escaped and its nose suggests it has caught a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: The deer suggests Rudolph, but the definition is the sign of a chill or a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddened nostril area is a common symptom of a chill or a heavy cold.

clue.text: Write down: 'Desist from wrapping snooker rod round mate's head'

indicators.note: the command wraps around everything else

parts.note: don't is the command to stop doing something

indicators.note: the stick goes round the single letter

parts.note: a cue is the stick used in snooker

indicators.note: only the first letter is used

parts.note: the word whose head is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop wrapping a snooker cue around a friend's head.
explanation.definitionFit: To document is to record something in writing, a synonym for noting it on paper.

clue.text: Under a misapprehension, take two days off and escape

indicators.note: with off, signals removing the letters
with take, the days are taken away

parts.note: someone deluded is labouring under a false belief
D is the abbreviation for day, so two days is a pair of them

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly takes a couple of days' leave and slips away.
explanation.walkthrough: DELUDED loses its first and last D to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to evade or escape from pursuit.

clue.text: Alpha male's last UV treatment is chaos

indicators.note: the letters are given a treatment that reorders them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the word whose final letter is used
taken as written

explanation.surface: A top male's final ultraviolet session at the tanning salon causes turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval is a violent disturbance or disruption, a state of great disorder.

clue.text: Detention is like the topping on a dessert, you might say!

indicators.note: the invented word is spoken, and its sound gives the answer

parts.words: like the topping on a dessert
parts.note: custard poured on a pudding, so custardy means like it

explanation.surface: Being kept in is compared to the sauce on a pudding, with an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: Custard is the yellow sauce poured over British puddings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held in custody means being detained by the police or the authorities.

clue.text: Wipe bum

definitions.meaning: first meaning: clean with a soft absorbent pad
second meaning: scrounge or cadge off others

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' seems to be a noun for the backside, but it is the verb to cadge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to clean with a soft pad and to live by cadging from others.

clue.text: Cry over old Welsh chicken

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits over the rest

parts.note: to yell is to cry out

explanation.surface: A shout goes up over an aged hen from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like a bird but is the adjective meaning cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is informal for cowardly, the same as chicken used as an adjective.

clue.text: Pop singer's after whip for a player

indicators.note: the singer's name follows the whip

parts.note: the cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip
Cher is the American pop singer

explanation.surface: A pop singer's next move is to swap a whip for a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcher is a fielder in baseball who receives the pitch, so one of the players.

clue.text: Beryl from south-east, gaining weight?

indicators.note: the compass letters gain the weight inside them

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A woman called Beryl from the south-east has put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Beryl looks like a woman's name; it is a mineral, the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is a mineral used as a gem, an example of a precious or semi-precious gem.

clue.text: Grains needing sun also

parts.note: and means also or in addition

explanation.surface: Crops need sunshine as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand is made of tiny particles of rock, so it consists of grains.

clue.text: Plant damaged — blame me on replacing 'earth' with 'live'

indicators.note: the words are broken up and their letters rearranged
one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: taken as written
E is the electrical symbol for earth
L is the electrical symbol for live

explanation.surface: A damaged plant leads someone to accept blame for swapping the earth wire for the live one.
explanation.walkthrough: Earth and live are wires in a British plug, marked E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon balm is a lemon-scented herb of the mint family, grown as a garden plant.

clue.text: See 18
Corporation backed energy that makes no noise

indicators.note: the word is read back to front

parts.note: corporation is jocular for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A company backed a silent form of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is old slang for a large paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Mute describes something that is silent or unable to produce sound.

clue.text: Almost grand, wearing community robe

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost

indicators.note: the town wears the letter inside it

parts.note: a town is a community

explanation.surface: A grand robe, almost, worn by a whole community.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown is a loose garment worn in bed, a kind of robe for sleeping.

clue.text: In short, possible Banksy work is set up

indicators.note: the phrase is abbreviated, keeping the ST of street

parts.note: Banksy is the anonymous British graffiti artist, so his work is street art

explanation.surface: Briefly, a Banksy piece may have been staged.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is the standard abbreviation for street.
explanation.definitionFit: To start a business is to set it up, i.e. to establish or found it.
